request.spec:
A sheet's children are the sheets naming it as their parent. The screen gains consolidated figures
over the sheet and all its descendants: the number of people, the due-total (each sheet's due-total
as that sheet shows it, added up) and the overdue-total (likewise). A sheet with no children shows
its own figures there.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A sheet's children are the sheets naming it as their parent. The screen gains consolidated figures

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures are in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. Getting there needed one change to existing behaviour that you should look at (below).

**What was built**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/descendants`, returns the sheet's children, their children, and so on. Each sheet appears once, and a loop of parent links can't make it run forever. The query is `SettingsRepository.descendants`, called from the new `LoadDescendants` and `RespondWithDescendants` classes and wired up in `rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/descendants.GET.yml`.
- **Screen:** a new panel, `features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`, sits just below the header. It shows `consolidated-people-count`, `consolidated-due-total` and `consolidated-overdue-total`. It works out each sheet's figures with the same code the header uses, so it adds up each sheet's totals exactly as that sheet's own header shows them. A sheet with no children shows its own figures.
- **Fresh data:** loading a sheet now also clears the stored copies of its descendants' data, so the totals are always re-read from the store, not taken from an earlier visit to a child sheet.

**Change to existing behaviour: editing a draft's date no longer moves its due-by.**
Scenario 2 failed at first, and not because of this feature. It edits a draft claim's date from 03-09 to 03-01 and expects the due-by to stay 2026-03-31, the date set when the claim was created. `SaveClaim.java` was deliberately recalculating the due-by from the new date (its comment said "a draft's due-by follows its date"), which gave 03-23. I changed it so the due-by stays as it was when the claim was created. That matches the test and the note in `useClaims.ts` that the due-by is fixed when the claim is created. If an earlier request relied on the due-by following the date, the two rules conflict and you'll need to pick one.

One run failed before the app started, because a library file couldn't be read. Nothing in the code caused it; the next run started normally and passed.
